item.title: Dudrich Mews-Flytipping-4th complaint-Legal Issues, 22nd September
item.description:
(First reported 28th August 2026) Failure to Remove 2 flytipped matresses To the Council and Enforcement Agency, It is acknowledged that Section 59(1) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 (EPA 1990) places a duty on landowners to clear waste. However, you have the legal authority—and a statutory duty—to enforce this. It has now been nearly four weeks since the mattresses were first reported on 28th August 2026, and they remain at the apartment entrance. To rectify this, it is requested that you immediately take the following two actions: **1. Use your enforcement powers under Section 59(2) of the EPA 1990** The law explicitly allows the council to serve a notice on the landowner/occupier requiring removal of the waste. If they fail to comply, you must enter the land, clear it, and recover your costs from them. **2. Use Section 215 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990** If the waste is adversely affecting the amenity of the area (which fly-tipping invariably does), you can serve a "Section 215 Notice" requiring the land to be cleaned up. Failure to comply is a criminal offence. **Regarding the "Private Land" excuse:** The Clean Neighbourhoods and Environment Act 2005 and subsequent case law confirm that councils cannot simply "close the case" because land is privately owned. Your duty to investigate the perpetrator (the tipper) remains active regardless of land ownership. *Conclusion:* If the waste constitutes a "statutory nuisance" (e.g., attracts rats, smells, or poses a health risk), you have a positive duty to act under the Environmental Protection Act 1990. Failure to do so constitutes maladministration, including failure to investigate/ remove the flytipped items amid potential criminal offences. This will be referred to the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman if the mattresses are not removed immediately. If the matresses are not removed by Friday 2nd October 2026. (8 working days), there will be a formal complaint issued.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Dudrich Mews, East Dulwich, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
